beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: Billionaires never sell their stock. So where's their cash?

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: It's a trick in three levels. And the last one is the one banks love.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: Easy. Sell $1,000,000 of shares and spend it.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: Sell, and the tax man takes $200,000 of that cash. Gone.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: So I never sell. I lock my shares at the bank as a promise, and borrow the cash instead.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: And the tax on that loan?

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: Zero tax. A loan isn't income. It just costs me $50,000 a year in interest.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: The cash buys me a yacht. The shares stay mine.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: Next year? I borrow again. The bank is happy to wait, because my shares keep growing.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: Level three: never sell. At an assumed 8% a year, my shares grow from $10,000,000 to $21.6M in 10 years.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: But if the market crashes, the bank won't wait. It sells my shares for me, at the worst price.

beats.speaker: sharma
beats.say: So the rich pick a small interest bill over a big tax bill. Cash borrowed, never sold.

beats.speaker: rohan
beats.say: So that's why billionaires never sell their stock.
